prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, in which many neutral atoms are interrogated at a magic wavelength, opening the regime of fractional frequency uncertainty near 1e-18

statement.case_for: I keep optical lattice clocks (B026) as my preferred configuration, and the first round has sharpened rather than weakened my reasons. The discovery content is a specific idea with a physical mechanism: at the magic wavelength the lattice light shifts the two clock levels equally, so thousands of neutral atoms can be held without perturbing the transition. Katori proposed this and demonstrated it; Ye's group then brought strontium lattice clocks to record stability and uncertainty near 1e-18 and used the many-atom platform to study collisional and many-body effects. Independent laboratories now operate such clocks and agree with each other and with the best ion clocks at the 1e-18 level, and that agreement is what makes a redefinition of the second, tests of time dilation over millimetres and clock-based geodesy real consequences. Two names correspond to two identifiable steps, so credit follows the decisive contributions without an arbitrary cut. I also now state the citation more precisely than in round 1, naming interrogation of many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength, so that what is new relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes is explicit in the text.
statement.case_against: The overlap objection is the one I must keep answering. The 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes are close neighbours, and a reader could take a lattice-clock prize as a third prize in precision timekeeping. I think the answer is that the new element is the engineered cancellation of the light shift for an ensemble, but that is a judgment, not a fact. The case also has narrower support than B009: three members ranked it, two first. I said in round 1 that seven members ranked B009 highly 'in part because it is the least objectionable common choice'. I cannot support that, because it attributes motives; the round-1 statements show that its supporters judge the physics on its merits, and I withdraw the remark. Finally, priority for the magic-wavelength proposal rests on my recollection, and the materials do not let me verify it or weigh the claims of other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups.

responses.point: Olsson argues that B009 is a distinct step beyond the 2016 prize, because 2016 concerned topological phase transitions and phases in model systems, whereas Kane-Mele and HgTe established a topological invariant of real band structures with a measurable edge signature.
responses.response: This persuades me on the incrementalism objection. I had been inclined to treat the 2016 overlap as a possible weakness of B009, and I now think it is answerable, in the same way I claim the 2005 and 2012 overlap is answerable for B026. I should not apply a stricter test to B009 than to my own candidate. What it does not answer is attribution. Hasan's 3D work and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal remain outside the trio, and your own text accepts that the citation must acknowledge them without crediting them. That is workable but it makes B009 the more contested configuration on credit, which is where I put the weight.

responses.point: Pearce moved from IceCube to B009 because convergence from condensed-matter, atomic and theory members reflects the case itself, and asks whether the 2025 circuit prize makes B010 ineligible or only a timing question.
responses.response: I accept that cross-field convergence is evidence about the case, and I would not dismiss the six-member position. On B010 I regard 2025 as a timing consideration, not a disqualification: the committee could return to circuit QED in a few years, and Girvin's absence from the trio would then need to be settled. My difference with you on B009 is that you call it the least problematic of the options on attribution. I would say B026 is less problematic, since the credited pair corresponds to the two decisive steps and no one in the shortlist has a claim that the pair displaces. You also ask for a citation that does not imply credit that cannot be given; I apply the same standard to my own and have written it around the lattice and magic-wavelength interrogation.

responses.point: Kroll says the separation from the comb and ion-control prizes must be made explicitly in the citation, that magic-wavelength priority is unverified, and that he sees the B009 versus B026 difference as partly about timing and credit clarity.
responses.response: I agree and have changed my citation as you suggested, adding the magic-wavelength interrogation of many neutral atoms. On the comparison with B009 I accept your reading: on the merits we are close, and the main difference is what each of us weighs when the credit is imperfect. I would also like to answer the chair's question directly: I treat B009 as an acceptable compromise if B026 does not carry, on the condition that the 2D versus 3D question is settled once and the omission of Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposers is stated openly. You have raised a recusal question related to John Hall; I do not know of any link between Hall's laboratory and my own work, and I would not object to your taking part.

responses.point: Mehlig asks whether the committee thinks clocks outrank a field that changed how condensed-matter theory classifies phases, and notes that support for clocks is narrow (three members, two first).
responses.response: I do not claim clocks outrank topological insulators in conceptual influence, and on that dimension B009 is ahead. The Nobel criterion is a discovery, invention or improvement of greatest benefit with credit that can be fairly assigned, and I place more weight on the second part when two candidates are close. The narrow support is real. I would not treat it as an argument in either direction, but I would ask the six B009 members whether the BHZ and Hasan gap is something they can defend to outside readers, since the three-name limit means we cannot repair it. If the committee decides it can, I will not stand in the way of B009.

responses.point: Johansson says a B037 prize should include theory (Jaksch-Zoller origin) and would rather accept the cost of omitting Esslinger than a configuration without theory, and that the committee should settle B009's 2D versus 3D question once.
responses.response: I agree with you on settling 2D versus 3D once and explicitly, because a B009 prize closes the topological-insulator question. On B037 you have moved me somewhat: I proposed an experimental trio in round 1, but the origin of the field in the Jaksch-Zoller proposal for the Bose-Hubbard model is a fair objection. I still think the allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac is too unsettled for B037 to be a first choice, and that Zoller and Cirac also recur in B030, which is why I keep it only as an alternative and not as my preferred configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that the lattice clock is a distinct achievement from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, a judgment I have argued but cannot verify.
Priority for the magic-wavelength proposal and the claims of other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups, which I recall from memory.
Whether a prize for B009 can be framed so that the omission of Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposers is stated fairly; if so, I would accept it as a close second.
Whether the committee will weigh breadth of support or clarity of credit more heavily when two candidates are scientifically close.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile. My documented collaborators are Anne L'Huillier, members of the Lund attosecond group, Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, Reinhold Schuch, J. Marcus Dahlstrom, Luca Argenti and Paul Indelicato, none of whom is credited on the shortlist. I work in atomic theory and have field proximity to the atomic and optical candidates B026, B037 and B030, which I disclose as scientific closeness and not a personal tie. I have no documented link to the credited names of B009, my first alternative. Update after round 1: I have no connection to Hall's laboratory that would bear on Kroll's flagged recusal question.
